name: Chaskiwasi relay station
summary: Chaskiwasi were small roadside houses on Inka roads where fresh runners waited to take over messages, the fixed relay posts of the chaski system.
description: Small roadside dwellings with replacement messengers, used as relay posts on selected Inka routes.
tier_reason: Relay facilities can be fine detail, but they are not the social practice itself. Archaeological identification limits remain. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

places.note: Andean regions of Tawantinsuyu (Inka empire), not limited to Peru and Chile
